newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Hesse sees differences with France on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Hesse sees differences with France on EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse said on Tuesday that France's proposal of a stability council to act as a counterweight to the European Central Bank illustrated there was still disharmony on some European issues between France and Germany.

In a speech to a new year's reception in Hamburg, Hesse quoted comments from French president Jacques Chirac and prime minister Alain Juppe expressing reservations about the level of power of the future central bank.
According to the text of his speech, which was released in advance, Hesse said such comments revealed that France was not ready to give up some forms of sovereignty.

"There is a lot pointing to the fact that France, where the belief in the overriding steering power of the centralised states is much more widespread than here in Germany, does ultimately not want to follow the functionalist route to European union under which "territorial sovereignty' will be given up and transferred as a "functional sovereignty' to a supranational body," Hesse said.

France had proposed the creation of a so-called stability council to act as a political counterweight to the European Central Bank, paying attention particularly to the external exchange rate of the euro.
Earlier, Bundesbank council member Olaf Sievert dismissed the French proposal, saying he saw no need for such a body.

In a speech prepared for delivery to a reception in the eastern German city of Leipzig, Sievert said that this appeared to be a meaningless attempt to find some form of mediator for monetary policy, which has the clearly defined role of maintaining price stability as its absolute priority.

"Of course, once the European Central Bank has the power to take the role which the Maastricht Treaties have given it, there may be some comfort in the fact that a stability council, which has nothing to decide, would only make a fool of itself if it hit on the idea of suggesting that the moon should go in the oposite direction from that which is ordained," he said.
"But why then bother with such a council at all," he added.
